name: Google Cloud API Design Guide
description: Style rules based on Google Cloud API Design Guide

rules.title: Use resource-oriented design
rules.rationale: APIs should be organized around resources, not actions.

judge.prompt: Check if the API follows resource-oriented design. Paths should be nouns representing resources, not verbs representing actions. Look for patterns like /resources/{id} rather than /getResource or /createResource.

rules.title: Use collection IDs
rules.rationale: Collection names should be plural and use camelCase.

judge.prompt: Check if collection names (the segments before resource IDs) are plural and use camelCase or lowercase. Examples: /users, /billingAccounts, /projects

rules.title: Resource hierarchy in path
rules.rationale: Resources should be organized hierarchically in the path.

judge.prompt: Check if related resources are organized hierarchically. Child resources should be nested under parent resources in the path, not passed as query parameters.

rules.title: Standard List method
rules.rationale: Collection endpoints should support GET for listing resources.

rules.title: Standard Get method
rules.rationale: Individual resources should support GET for retrieval.

judge.prompt: Check if paths with resource IDs (e.g., /users/{userId}) support GET method for retrieving individual resources.

rules.title: Standard Create method
rules.rationale: Collection endpoints should support POST for creating resources.

judge.prompt: Check if collection paths support POST for creating new resources.

rules.title: Standard Update method with PATCH
rules.rationale: Use PATCH for partial updates, PUT for full replacement.

judge.prompt: Check if PATCH is used for partial updates. Google recommends PATCH with field masks over PUT for updates.

rules.title: Standard Delete method
rules.rationale: Individual resources should support DELETE for removal.

judge.prompt: Check if resource paths support DELETE method for removing resources.

rules.title: Custom methods use colon syntax
rules.rationale: Custom methods should use resource:verb pattern.

judge.prompt: Check if custom (non-CRUD) operations use the colon syntax: /resource:action. For example, /documents/{doc}:translate instead of /translateDocument.

rules.title: Custom methods use POST
rules.rationale: Custom methods should use POST HTTP verb.

judge.prompt: Check if custom methods (those with colon syntax or action verbs) use POST. Only use GET for custom methods that are idempotent and have no side effects.

rules.title: Use snake_case for field names
rules.rationale: JSON field names should use snake_case per Google style.

rules.title: Use consistent time field names
rules.rationale: Time fields should use _time suffix (e.g., create_time, update_time).

judge.prompt: Check if timestamp fields use the _time suffix pattern: create_time, update_time, delete_time, expire_time. Not createdAt or timestamp.

rules.title: Use singular resource names for types
rules.rationale: Schema/message names should be singular nouns.

judge.prompt: Check if schema names are singular (User, Project, Instance) rather than plural (Users, Projects, Instances).

rules.title: Use standard Google error format
rules.rationale: Error responses should follow Google's standard error format.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses use Google's error format: {"error": {"code": number, "message": string, "status": string, "details": []}}

rules.title: Use canonical error codes
rules.rationale: Use Google's canonical error codes (INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, etc.).

judge.prompt: Check if error codes reference canonical codes like INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_EXISTS, PERMISSION_DENIED, etc.

rules.title: Operations have summaries
rules.rationale: All operations should have summary descriptions.

rules.title: Parameters have descriptions
rules.rationale: All parameters should be documented.

rules.title: Schemas have descriptions
rules.rationale: Schema types should have descriptions.

rules.title: Include version in path
rules.rationale: API version should be in the URL path.

rules.title: Use v1, v2, etc. format
rules.rationale: Major versions should be v1, v2, etc. Pre-release can be v1alpha, v1beta.

judge.prompt: Check if API versions follow Google patterns: v1, v2 for stable; v1alpha, v1beta for pre-release. Not 1.0, 2024-01-01, etc.
